# Labour Party Manifesto 2024: A Summary

## Change and National Renewal

This manifesto presents Labour's vision for ending Conservative "chaos" and beginning national renewal through a partnership between government, business, and working people. The central premise is that 14 years of Conservative rule have damaged Britain's economy, public services, and standing in the world, while breaking the promise that hard work leads to fair reward.

## Strong Foundations

Labour's approach rests on three pillars: **national security** (maintaining NATO commitment, nuclear deterrent, and addressing new threats including cyber warfare); **secure borders** (creating a Border Security Command to tackle criminal smuggling gangs rather than the "unworkable" Rwanda scheme); and **economic stability** (non-negotiable fiscal rules ensuring balanced budgets and falling debt).

## Five National Missions

**Kickstart Economic Growth**: Labour will pursue a strategic partnership with business through a new industrial strategy, establish a £7.3 billion National Wealth Fund to attract private investment, reform planning to build 1.5 million homes, and devolve power to local leaders through "Local Growth Plans." The party will cap corporation tax at 25%, reform business rates, and implement the "New Deal for Working People" including banning zero-hours contracts and strengthening workers' rights.

**Clean Energy Superpower**: Labour commits to clean power by 2030 through Great British Energy, a publicly-owned company headquartered in Scotland. This includes doubling onshore wind, tripling solar, and quadrupling offshore wind. A £6.6 billion Warm Homes Plan will upgrade five million homes. No new oil and gas exploration licences will be issued, though existing production continues.

**Take Back Our Streets**: A Neighbourhood Policing Guarantee will restore visible community policing. Labour aims to halve knife crime within a decade and halve violence against women and girls, with specialist rape units in every police force and fast-tracked rape cases through dedicated courts.

**Break Down Barriers to Opportunity**: Investment in education includes 6,500 new teachers, 3,000 primary school nurseries, free breakfast clubs, and reformed assessment. Labour will abolish VAT exemptions for private schools to fund state education, establish Skills England, and reform the apprenticeship levy into a "Growth and Skills Levy."

**NHS Fit for the Future**: Two million additional appointments annually, 8,500 new mental health staff, doubled cancer scanners, and a Dentistry Rescue Plan. Labour will shift towards prevention and community-based care, work towards a National Care Service with national standards, and maintain the NHS as publicly owned and funded.

## Political Reform and International Relations

Labour will establish an Ethics and Integrity Commission, remove hereditary peers, introduce mandatory retirement at 80 for Lords, and give 16-17 year-olds the vote. Relations with devolved governments will be reset through a new Council of Nations and Regions.

Internationally, Labour will maintain the US alliance whilst rebuilding European relationships through a new UK-EU security pact—without rejoining the single market. Britain will return to climate leadership and support Ukraine, whilst recognising Palestinian statehood as part of a two-state solution.

## Conclusion

The manifesto frames this election as a choice between continued Conservative chaos and Labour's disciplined, mission-driven approach to rebuilding Britain—with fiscal responsibility, partnership with business, and service to working people at its core.
